name: LP-relaxation bound and ratio-greedy for knapsack
statement: Sorting items by value/weight and filling greedily with a fractional last item solves the LP relaxation; its value is an upper bound on the integer optimum, and greedy plus the best single item gets at least half of optimum
business_use: Fast bound and warm start for any budgeted selection: features, projects, SKUs, campaigns

name: Knapsack FPTAS
statement: Profit scaling plus dynamic programming gives a (1-epsilon)-approximation in time polynomial in n and 1/epsilon
business_use: Near-optimal selection at very large scale with a quantified loss

name: Greedy submodular maximization (1-1/e)
statement: For monotone submodular objectives with a cardinality constraint, greedy selection achieves at least (1-1/e) of optimum; the same factor holds under a knapsack constraint with enumeration
business_use: Selecting campaigns, influencers, sensors, tests or sites when overlapping value has diminishing returns

name: Knapsack-constrained submodular (1-1/e)
statement: Partial enumeration plus greedy attains (1-1/e) for monotone submodular maximization under a knapsack budget
business_use: Cost-weighted selection with overlap penalties

name: Markowitz efficient frontier
statement: For a given expected return, the minimum-variance portfolio lies on a quadratic-programming frontier; diversification lowers variance when correlation is below one
business_use: Allocating capital, suppliers, channels or R and D bets under risk

name: CVaR linear programming formulation
statement: Conditional value-at-risk of a portfolio can be minimized by a linear program over scenarios
business_use: Tail-risk-aware allocation and hedging

name: Kelly criterion
statement: Betting the fraction that maximizes expected log wealth maximizes long-run growth rate
business_use: Sizing repeated bets or experiments with bankroll constraints

name: Equimarginal principle (KKT)
statement: At an optimum of a separable concave allocation, the marginal return per unit of budget is equal across all funded options
business_use: Splitting ad, R and D, cloud or grant budgets

name: Dorfman-Steiner theorem
statement: Optimal advertising-to-revenue ratio equals advertising elasticity divided by the absolute price elasticity of demand
business_use: Sizing marketing budgets and price-advertising mix

name: LP duality and shadow prices
statement: Each constraint has a dual price equal to the marginal objective gain from one more unit of that resource
business_use: Value of extra budget, capacity, headcount or time

name: Bellman principle of optimality
statement: An optimal multi-stage policy has optimal sub-policies from every reachable state
business_use: Dynamic programming for sequential allocation, replenishment and pricing

name: Lagrangian relaxation bound
statement: Dualizing hard constraints gives a lower (or upper) bound and heuristics, with the gap measuring solution quality
business_use: Bounding large integer models and decomposing by resource

name: Graham list scheduling bound
statement: Any list schedule on m identical machines has makespan at most (2-1/m) times optimal
business_use: Dependable baseline for production, ticket and job scheduling

name: Smith rule (WSPT)
statement: Sequencing jobs by weight over processing time minimizes total weighted completion time on a single machine
business_use: Prioritizing jobs, tickets, repairs and orders

name: Johnson rule
statement: Sequencing two-machine flow shop jobs with Johnson's rule minimizes makespan
business_use: Two-stage production, review or approval pipelines

name: Unrelated machines 2-approximation
statement: LP rounding yields makespan at most twice optimal, and no polynomial algorithm can beat 3/2 unless P=NP
business_use: Assigning work to non-identical resources

name: Hungarian algorithm / assignment integrality
statement: The assignment LP has integral optimal solutions and is solved exactly in polynomial time
business_use: Matching staff, tickets, trucks, shows or territories one-to-one

name: Birkhoff-von Neumann theorem
statement: Doubly stochastic matrices are convex combinations of permutation matrices
business_use: Why relaxing assignment to an LP still returns a valid matching

name: Gale-Shapley stable matching
statement: A stable matching always exists and the deferred-acceptance algorithm finds it
business_use: Matching with preferences on both sides: hiring, volunteers, programs

name: Max-flow min-cut
statement: The maximum flow through a network equals the minimum capacity cut
business_use: Flow-based assignment, transportation and capacity feasibility checks

name: Hakimi vertex theorem
statement: An optimal 1-median or p-median location exists at a network vertex
business_use: Reduces site selection to a finite set of candidate locations

name: Metric facility location approximation
statement: LP rounding gives a constant-factor approximation (about 3.16) for metric uncapacitated facility location
business_use: Large-scale site selection with guaranteed quality

name: k-center 2-approximation
statement: Farthest-first traversal is a 2-approximation for k-center and no better factor is possible unless P=NP
business_use: Minimax service-distance siting such as clinics or ambulances

name: Greedy set cover H(n) bound
statement: Greedy cost-effectiveness selection is within a harmonic-number factor (about ln n) of optimum
business_use: Covering demand, threats, audiences or test requirements cheaply

name: Set cover inapproximability
statement: No polynomial algorithm beats about ln n for set cover unless NP has quasi-polynomial algorithms
business_use: Explains why greedy is essentially the best worst-case guarantee

name: NP-completeness of selection problems
statement: Knapsack, set cover and many scheduling and routing decision problems are NP-complete
business_use: Justifies heuristics and time-limited exact solvers at scale

name: Economic order quantity
statement: Minimizing ordering plus holding cost gives Q* = sqrt(2DK/h)
business_use: Baseline order size for stable demand

name: (s,S) optimality
statement: With fixed ordering cost and convex holding/shortage cost, a reorder-point/order-up-to policy is optimal
business_use: Replenishment policy for stochastic inventory

name: Newsvendor critical fractile
statement: The optimal single-period order quantity is the demand quantile at cost ratio Cu/(Cu+Co)
business_use: Perishables, seasonal goods and one-shot buys

name: Echelon base-stock optimality
statement: In serial multi-echelon systems, echelon base-stock policies are optimal and decomposable
business_use: Multi-location safety stock

name: Wagner-Whitin lot sizing
statement: Dynamic programming finds the optimal order plan for time-varying demand with setup and holding costs
business_use: Production and purchase timing

name: Little's law
statement: Average work in system equals throughput times average time in system
business_use: Sizing queues, beds, inventories and support backlogs

name: Dynamic pricing with finite stock
statement: Optimal price falls with remaining time and rises with remaining inventory under intensity-control models
business_use: Markdown and revenue management

name: Gordon-Loeb rule
statement: Optimal security investment is at most 1/e (about 37 percent) of the expected loss from a breach
business_use: Sizing cybersecurity and continuity budgets

name: Mossin theorem on insurance
statement: If the premium has a positive loading, full insurance is not optimal for a risk-averse buyer
business_use: Choosing coverage levels and deductibles

name: Baumol square-root rule
statement: Optimal cash conversion size is proportional to the square root of cash need times transaction cost over interest rate
business_use: Liquidity management

name: Gittins index theorem
statement: For independent bandit arms with discounting, playing the highest-index arm is optimal
business_use: Allocating effort between known and unknown options as trends evolve

name: UCB logarithmic regret
statement: The UCB1 policy achieves regret that grows only logarithmically in time
business_use: Learning which channels, tests or offers perform while spending

name: Rolling-horizon optimality
statement: Re-solving a finite-horizon model each period is near optimal under stated conditions
business_use: Planning in fast-changing, trend-sensitive settings

name: Robust budget of uncertainty
statement: Allowing at most Gamma coefficients to deviate keeps the robust counterpart a linear program with probabilistic guarantees
business_use: Planning under uncertain demand, costs and lead times

name: Bass diffusion model
statement: Adoption rate combines innovation and imitation, producing a rise-and-decay curve
business_use: Forecasting trend lifetimes for timing and funding

name: Influence spread submodularity
statement: Expected cascade size in standard diffusion models is monotone submodular
business_use: Why greedy seeding works for influencer and referral selection

name: AdWords (1-1/e) competitive ratio
statement: A balance-type online algorithm is (1-1/e)-competitive for allocating budgeted ads
business_use: Online budget-constrained allocation

name: Price of fairness
statement: Imposing fairness constraints reduces total efficiency by a quantifiable factor
business_use: Fair bonus pools, scholarships and workload balancing
